- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply 2–4% downward adjustment for first 7 days.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative; forecast should align with 14-day moving average if sentiment < 0.50.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.67 → -0.33 → +0.67), model often fails to adjust; apply 3–5% downward correction after 2nd reversal.
